title: Netflix Reworks Conductor for 420 Million Monthly Workflow Executions and 10X Larger Workflows
gist: Netflix's Conductor 4.0 rewrite lifts max workflow size from ~2,500 to 30,000 tasks and cuts p99 evaluation latency ~40% by separating workflow metadata from task data and removing locks, at a scale of ~200,000 workflow definitions, 150 applications and ~420 million executions per month — with demand expected to grow fivefold as Netflix pushes into live content, games and podcasts.

insights.claim: Netflix's Conductor workflow orchestration engine now supports roughly 200,000 workflow definitions across 150 applications and executes about 420 million workflows per month.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Concrete benchmark for what 'hyperscale orchestration' means — useful for sizing the durable-execution market against vendors like Temporal.
insights.locator: Netflix has reworked its Conductor workflow orchestration

insights.claim: The Conductor redesign increases supported workflow size from approximately 2,500 to 30,000 tasks while reducing p99 workflow evaluation latency by about 40%.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A 10x ceiling increase signals workloads (AI pipelines, media processing) that previously had to be split are now single-workflow addressable.
insights.locator: The redesign increases the supported workflow size

insights.claim: Conductor orchestrates distributed workflows across Netflix's Content and Studio Engineering, Ads, and Games organizations, indicating workflow orchestration has become horizontal internal infrastructure rather than a single-team tool.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Orchestration is consolidating as a platform layer inside large tech firms — buy-vs-build decisions shift toward centralized engines.

insights.claim: Netflix expects workflow demand to potentially grow fivefold as it expands into areas including live content, games and podcasts.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A stated 5x internal compute/orchestration growth path tied directly to Netflix's live, gaming and podcast expansion strategy.
insights.locator: Netflix expects workflow demand to potentially grow fivefold

insights.claim: Conductor's evolution involved migrating execution data from Dynomite to Cassandra, moving large task inputs and outputs to Amazon S3, and replacing DynoQueues with Timestone.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Shows the repeated pattern of offloading large payloads to object storage — reinforces S3-class storage as the default substrate for stateful systems.
insights.locator: Its evolution included migrating execution data

insights.claim: Kafka was introduced to decouple indexing from the execution path, with Elasticsearch and Iceberg supporting indexing and long-term storage of workflow data.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Iceberg keeps appearing as the long-term table format of choice at hyperscale, strengthening the open-lakehouse standard.
insights.locator: Kafka was later introduced to decouple indexing

insights.claim: Earlier Conductor versions loaded complete workflow state into memory during evaluation, which created memory pressure as workflows grew; the new design separates workflow metadata from task and user data and loads only the task data needed for the next decision using a lightweight workflow blueprint.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: The general lesson — lazy, partial state loading beats whole-object materialization — is the core scaling unlock for stateful orchestration products.
insights.locator: With Conductor 4.0, Netflix identified workflow evaluation

insights.claim: The redesign removes locking from task state coordination by storing pending and terminal task states separately and reconciling them in the application layer, with terminal state taking precedence.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A reusable pattern: replace distributed locks with separated state plus application-layer reconciliation to escape contention ceilings.
insights.locator: The redesign also removes locking from task state

insights.claim: Netflix reports that failed lock acquisition attempts, which reached about 2,700 per interval during contention, dropped to essentially zero after workflow evaluation was moved out of the synchronous request path into exclusive Timestone queues processed sequentially and asynchronously.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Quantifies how much headroom asynchronous, queue-partitioned evaluation unlocks versus synchronous locking designs.
insights.locator: Netflix reports that failed lock acquisition attempts

insights.claim: In a 2022 Conductor community discussion, a user reported 55,745 workflows and 310,000 tasks driving JVM heap usage to 5 GB, and maintainer Aravind Ramkumar explained the engine loaded the entire running workflow into memory for evaluation.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: The architectural flaw was publicly visible four years before the fix — a reminder that OSS issue trackers leak roadmap and risk signals early.
insights.locator: Earlier Conductor community discussions had surfaced

insights.claim: Another 2022 discussion described a 1.7 MB workflow containing nearly 5,000 task entries where storing the workflow definition took close to two minutes and repeatedly loading it from the database affected execution time.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Illustrates how metadata size, not just execution volume, becomes the binding constraint in orchestration engines.
insights.locator: Another 2022 discussion described a 1.7 MB workflow

insights.claim: When a user reported 25,000 to 30,000 running workflows with HTTP task queues building up, maintainer Ramkumar advised that increasing polling counts would not improve processing and could overload the system, recommending horizontal scaling instead.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Counterintuitive operational rule — more polling makes throughput worse — matters for anyone sizing agent/worker fleets.
insights.locator: Earlier discussions also highlighted worker scaling constraints

insights.claim: Netflix discontinued maintenance of its public Conductor OSS repository in December 2023, citing a shift toward its internal Conductor fork, while community-contributed modules and extensions remain in a separate community repository.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Another instance of a hyperscaler pulling core infrastructure back in-house — creates openings for commercial orchestration vendors serving the abandoned user base.
insights.locator: Netflix discontinued maintenance of its public Conductor OSS

insights.claim: Conductor 4.0 adds native concurrency controls, dynamic worker allocation, and a type-safe Java Workflow SDK already used by Netflix Ads for creative ingestion and Data Clean Room workflows.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Data Clean Room workflows at Netflix Ads signal the advertising stack's growing dependence on privacy-preserving orchestration.
